messages:
maya: :rotating_light: heads up — multiple support tickets and synthetic alerts showing surge of 504s and gateway timeouts from hosted inference in eu-west1a starting ~09:15 UTC. Customers: several mid-market PLG apps and a couple of internal smoke tests. Logs show 502/504 from our gateway and backend gRPC timeouts. attaching initial snippets below.

cs-jordan: Seeing 8 customer escalations opened since 09:18. All reporting inference requests stall ~2–10s then 504. Example customer req_id: rq_6f2c3e. They want ETA and repro steps.

devon: Oncall checking the api-gateway pods and host metrics. No obvious CPU/GPU pressure. Gateway logs show lots of "upstream connect error" and "upstream request timeout". Can someone run network path checks to the eu-west1a edge?

neteng-lee: Running mtr and tcpdump now. Early signs point to packet reordering and a small burst of packet loss on the primary provider path into eu-west1a — not full outage but enough to cause TCP retransmit/backoff and long tail latencies. Provider AS shows a recent micro-flap.

neteng-lee: pasted traceroute (shortened):
```
traceroute to eu-west1a-edge (203.0.113.45), 30 hops max
 1  10.1.5.1  0.3 ms
 2  198.51.100.12  2.2 ms
 3  203.0.113.201  12.8 ms  35.0 ms  11.9 ms
 4  * * *
 5  198.51.200.7  120 ms  11 ms  122 ms
```
You can see high variance and out-of-order replies — classic reordering.

devon: Interesting — our gateway uses short timeouts on upstream gRPC to avoid queued requests; with reordering we hit timeouts frequently. Can we reroute traffic to eu-west1b while provider works on path?

ops-ravi: We can shift a fraction of traffic via routing policy to eu-west1b. Doing a canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% with gradual increase to avoid cascades. Initiating at 09:40 UTC. Will post progress.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0345 (automated). Runbook: /runbooks/network-path-degradation. Assigned: neteng-lee, devon, ops-ravi.

devon: Quick repro steps for engineers and CS: 1) curl our hosted endpoint with a streaming payload, 2) observe gateway logs for upstream connect errors and message: "upstream request timeout". Example: 
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED' \\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
If you see repeated timeouts + high retransmit counts on tcpdump it's likely packet reordering.

neteng-lee: Confirmed provider has a transient AS path change at ~09:12 UTC with ECMP oscillation between two transit peers causing reordering. They've acknowledged and are working a fix but no ETA. We're maintaining the diversion route to eu-west1b and also adding short-term TCP tuning on gateway (increase max_retries, small increase in upstream timeout) to reduce surface area.

cs-jordan: Messaging customers: preparing templated update: we cite network path instability in eu-west1a, mitigation in progress (traffic reroute + gateway timeout adjustment). ETA: monitoring and follow-up in 30m.

maya: Thanks — prioritize customers with high SLAs. Devon/ops, after reroute show grafana snapshots of 95/99th latency before/after so I can include in the update.

ops-ravi: Canary started 09:40 UTC -> 10% traffic. 09:50 -> 50%. 10:05 UTC -> 90%. 10:12 UTC -> 100% divert to eu-west1b. Observability: backlog of 504s dropped by 86% after 50% shift.

devon: Pushed gateway config to bump upstream timeout from 1.5s -> 2.5s and set retry count 2 -> 3 (short term). Need to watch tokenized rate/cost effects.

neteng-lee: Provider reports they deployed a fix at 10:20 UTC and BGP paths stabilized — but we already completed reroute. Recommend we keep the reroute for 30m and then slowly shift back.

maya: Ok, action items: cs-jordan send customer update (10:30), neteng-lee confirm path stable and propose rollback plan, devon monitor error budget and revert gateway timeout after rollback, ops-ravi coordinate traffic shift back 10:50 -> 11:10 window.

cs-jordan: Customer update posted at 10:33 UTC: short note + link to incident. Customers replied :thumbsup: for transparency.

neteng-lee: Running a final mtr now — paths clean, no reordering for 10m. Preparing timeline for postmortem.

maya: Marking this as mitigated at 11:00 UTC but keeping incident open for postmortem and follow-up with provider. Thanks all. :tada:
